title.value: Descent Reckoned Through Starter: Ferment Lineage and the Division of the Culture Among the Anchor Terrace Households

abstract.value: Among the Anchor Terrace Households, kinship is reckoned through the inheritance of living pit cultures rather than through bodies. We record forty-one divisions of the culture over two seasons and show that a household states its position in the terrace as the number of divisions separating its starter from a named ancestral pit. A household whose culture dies is not orphaned but dissolved, and the term used for the event is the same term used for a spoiled draw. We argue that where the transmitted substance is alive, descent is best treated as a property of the substance and not of the people carrying it.
